top_choice_rationale: P001 (B001: Pakes, Berry, Levinsohn) is a mature measurement advance. It recovers substitution patterns, markups and welfare counterfactuals from market data with endogenous prices, which earlier reduced-form work could not do. It has about three decades of use in merger review and regulation and has spread to trade, health and environmental economics. Its main sensitivities (numerics, instruments, functional form) are documented. The credit is compact because the core 1995 paper has three authors, so a three-laureate cap fits without splitting it. The residual costs are the omission of Bresnahan, Reiss, Benkard and Levin and the toolkit-versus-discovery judgement. These are matters of citation framing and not of merit, and they do not outweigh awarding a clearly deserving, mature achievement over no award. The citation should stay at method level and not overstate robustness. My assessment rests on background knowledge and the committee exchange, not independent verification.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; no tie to Pakes, Berry or Levinsohn. Disclosed but not adjudicated: SSE affiliation alongside committee colleagues, and the 2020 presentation speech, which does not establish a personal preference.
